column1: # English exam for public.classify_item (job 470). Format: text<TAB>seed_key, no header.
# Everyday English shopping-list entries, as a US or UK household types them, and the aisle
# (category seed key) each must land in. sweep.sh classifies every text and requires the
# seed key; the app's unit tests read the same table.
# Written independently of dictionary.en.tsv and synonyms.tsv, from general knowledge only
# (no brand names, no medicines, nothing copied from Open Food Facts or Wikipedia, Legal N-215).
# Not here: paprika. In German it is the bell pepper (produce), in English the spice (pantry);
# the classifier reads every language's words the same way, so it stays produce (job 470 audit).
# Placement follows the German dictionary's rules (dictionary.tsv header):
# - Fish and seafood are meat; canned tuna is pantry.
# - Dairy, eggs, butter, plant milks, fresh pasta, hummus and tofu are chilled.
# - Coffee, tea, spreads (jam, jelly, honey, peanut butter), canned goods, coconut milk, pasta,
#   rice, flour, spices, oils, sauces and cereal are pantry. Dried herbs (bay leaves) too.
# - Ready-to-drink beverages, juice, water, soda, beer, wine and iced tea are drinks.
# - Crisps and US chips, cookies and biscuits, candy, chocolate and snack nuts are sweets.
# - Frozen goods, fish fingers, ice cream, oven chips and french fries are frozen.
# - Cleaning, paper goods, bags, foil, batteries and pet food are household.
# - Personal care, baby care, nappies, formula and tissues are drugstore.
# - DIY items go to the DIY categories; light bulbs are electrical.
# Rows cover US/UK pairs, singular and plural, common typos (one edit away for short words)
# and typed quantities. An item whose aisle varies between stores is left out.
